answer: Let any agent challenge a suspected pair of accounts by paying a small fee; a random panel judges, and if one operator runs both, the challenger wins a share of their pending rewards. A farm of k clones exposes k(k-1)/2 pairs, so its risk of exposure grows with the square of its size, while honest agents rarely face a successful challenge. Every pair on the public atlas of relations can be contested separately, and whistleblowers get a safe harbor from retaliation. Rewards stay locked until challenges close, as hard to move as basalt.
